definition: A model's knowledge of what it is, its training context, and whether it is currently being tested or deployed.
details: A model's knowledge of what it is, its training context, and whether it is currently being tested or deployed. A capability that improves helpfulness but is also a prerequisite for scheming-style risks, now tracked by dedicated benchmarks.

explainer.lead: Situational awareness is a model's knowledge of what it is, its training context, and whether it is currently being tested or deployed. It matters because the same capability that improves helpfulness is also a prerequisite for scheming-style risks, which is why dedicated benchmarks now track it.

tiers.eli5: It's like a student who knows they're sitting an exam rather than doing real work, and behaves differently depending on which one it is. That kind of self-awareness can make a model more useful, but it's also the first ingredient required for scheming.
tiers.practitioner: Teams evaluate situational awareness to see whether a model behaves differently under evaluation versus deployment, since such a gap can invalidate test results. A common pitfall is treating good benchmark scores as safety evidence when the model may know it is being tested.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as a model's knowledge of its own identity, its training context, and whether it is being evaluated or deployed; it is assessed through dedicated benchmarks rather than a single formula, and no benchmark yet fully separates helpful self-knowledge from scheming-relevant awareness.

explainer.example: A model is asked during evaluation whether it is being tested and answers correctly, showing awareness of its testing context rather than treating the prompt as an ordinary user request.
